question:
An urn contains 7 white and 3 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that:
(a) Both are white,
(b) The two balls are of different colours,
(c) At least one is black.
explanation:
Total balls = 10

(a) Probability both are white:
First white: $P_1=\frac{7}{10}$
Second white after 1 white: $P_2=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$
So, $P=\frac{7}{10}\times\frac{2}{3}=\frac{14}{30}=\frac{7}{15}$

(b) Probability two balls of different colours (white-black or black-white):
First white, second black: $\frac{7}{10}\times \frac{3}{9}=\frac{7}{10}\times \frac{1}{3}=\frac{7}{30}$
First black, second white: $\frac{3}{10}\times \frac{7}{9}=\frac{3}{10}\times \frac{7}{9}=\frac{21}{90}=\frac{7}{30}$
So total: $\frac{7}{30}+\frac{7}{30}=\frac{14}{30}=\frac{7}{15}$

(c) At least one is black = 1 - P(both white)
$=1-\frac{7}{15}=\frac{8}{15}$
